jonny-desktop.task: context-keeper: adopt CLAUDE.md-doc findings - .claude/rules/ scoped-constraint projection, PreToolUse scope_guard (rule arrives before the edit), summary truncation floor, README positioning vs auto memory
jonny-desktop.note: DONE + PUSHED (2 commits). PR #13 updated with f6d1fe1. Follow-up to the PreToolUse move: measured the cost the move introduced rather than assuming it was fine. 142ms per Edit/Write on Windows, of which 73ms was `import server` (mirror -> urllib.request -> http.client -> email.parser, plus secrets/usage/code_drift) and only ~9ms was real work; a path matching NO constraint paid the same 142ms as a hit, which is most edits. Extracted store_paths.py (json + os only) holding project resolution and raw reads; server.py now imports its resolution from there so the precedence order has exactly one implementation. Result 142ms -> 69ms against a 62ms bare-interpreter floor - the remainder is Python process startup, unavoidable for a shell hook. Added TestEditPathHookCost pinning the PROPERTY not the number (fails if an edit-path hook imports server, if store_paths grows an import past json/os, or if the two resolution impls stop being the same object), and verified it fails by deliberately re-adding `import server`. Two things the existing tests caught during the refactor and were right to: TestStaleIndexWrites (server.read_json_file had to stay a wrapper, not an import, or half its reads route past the patch point the race test uses) and TestPackagingCompleteness (store_paths.py missing from sdist/wheel/mcpb staging - the check that exists because semantic_index.py once shipped missing). Also wired ~/.claude/settings.json to PreToolUse with timeout 5, live for every project on this machine; backup at ~/.claude/settings.json.bak-pretooluse. 395 tests pass, was 392. Recorded con-010-acde (origin user, enforced_by TestEditPathHookCost). Next action: review and squash-merge PR #13.
